name: Ophrah
overview: Ophrah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Meonothai. His mention in Scripture is concise, with no additional notes expanding on his life or deeds beyond his genealogy. This brief record situates him within the genealogical framework of Judah's descendants.
namesAndTitles: The name Ophrah means "young gazelle" in Hebrew, reflecting a common biblical practice of meaningful proper names. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it carries a natural imagery that may symbolize grace or swiftness. This is the sole name recorded for him.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ophrah as the son of Meonothai, establishing a direct paternal link. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text for Ophrah.
scriptureSignificance: Ophrah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah, a tribe central to God's redemptive plan culminating in Christ. His mention underscores the faithfulness of God's promises to preserve the lineage through which the Messiah would come. While not elaborated upon, such genealogical entries affirm the historical and spiritual continuity of God's covenant people.
